question:
Create a new KiCad project named b28 in the project directory and draw its schematic for the following request.

Build a USB-C ATmega32U4-M development module with castellated Pro Micro-style interfaces. Use a 16 MHz crystal, USBLC6-2P6 USB ESD protection, 22 ohm USB series resistors, a 500 mA polyfuse and a Schottky feed from fused RAW to VCC. Include reset pull-up, HWB grounded, USB-C sink resistors and the MCU's normal supply/UCAP/AREF bypassing. Expose raw USB D+/D- on a separate two-pad connector.
The custom castellated headers must use these pin orders. First 12-pad row: RAW, GND, RESET, VCC, PF4, PF5, PF6, PF7, PB1, PB3, PB2, PB6. Second 12-pad row: PB5, PB4, PE6, PD7, PC6, PD4, PD0, PD1, GND, GND, PD2, PD3. Extra 5-pad row: PF0, PF1, PC7, PD5, PB7. Use the supplied castellated and USB-C footprints. VCC is diode-fed; no 3.3 V regulator is fitted.
Local dependencies: Use the project-local footprint libraries in lib/ under the project directory (goldfish-pins.pretty, goldfish.pretty and molex-216990_gct-usb45xx_hro-type-c-31-m-13x.pretty); use standard KiCad libraries for everything else.
